articles.title: Poury supplies the points; Mossdeep secures the bye
articles.dek: Holt scored through the air and on the ground in a 27–3 win over Sunyshore. The Eclipse are 15–0, with the conference’s first seed secured and a second-quarter review waiting.
articles.author: mara-voss

body.text: Poury Holt caught a twelve-yard touchdown pass on Mossdeep’s first possession and ran seven yards for another score late in the third quarter. Between those plays, the Eclipse gave Sunyshore very little room to build an answer. Mossdeep won 27–3, improved to 15–0 and secured the Hoenn–Sinnoh conference’s first seed and postseason bye. The Starseekers left with 170 total yards, one field goal and a much clearer account of the work a return visit would require.

Holt finished with 121 yards on eighteen carries and caught all three of his targets for forty-seven more. Dram Marino completed twenty-one of twenty-six passes for 316 yards and two touchdowns, adding a one-yard rushing score. Ninjulio Jones caught six passes for 126 yards. Mossdeep converted five of seven third downs, produced twenty-two first downs and held the ball for the final 4:54 without allowing another Sunyshore possession.

Michael Dorrill had plenty to recognize. He also had two punts, an interception and a missed extra point to discuss. A scoreless second quarter had interrupted a thirteen-point opening period, leaving the visitors within ten at halftime. The Eclipse’s defense kept that interruption from becoming a serious threat, but Dorrill’s standards do not depend on the other team making him pay immediately.

“We earned the bye. Good. Now pull up the second quarter,” Dorrill said. “Two punts and a ball thrown to the other team. Everybody can enjoy the standings after they explain those possessions. We have two more games before the playoffs, and neither opponent is responsible for improving our execution.”
Holt made the early opportunities count

Mossdeep’s first offensive snap produced a forty-two-yard completion deep right from Marino to Accel BeckhmJr. Holt followed with two three-yard runs left, then caught the short-right throw on third-and-four for the opening touchdown at 4:07. A missed extra point kept the score at 6–0. The drive covered sixty yards in four plays and gave Sunyshore an immediate example of the problem: protecting against the deep receiver still left a useful back available underneath.

The next Eclipse possession traveled eighty-four yards in eight plays. Marino finished it himself, running up the middle from one yard with a minute left in the first quarter. Adam Vinathorn made the extra point for a 13–0 lead. Sunyshore had punted on its first two possessions and would punt again before the quarter ended. The Starseekers were already having to win several consecutive exchanges merely to get back into a competitive position.

Holt’s contribution deserves attention beyond the two scoring entries. His receiving gains came on three targets, so Mossdeep obtained forty-seven yards without an incompletion on those throws. His rushing work averaged 6.7 yards per carry. Those are distinct jobs, and he completed both against an opponent that entered the afternoon with eleven wins. Holt’s combination of rushing and receiving production helped Mossdeep sustain drives against one of the conference’s strongest opponents.

“If I’m carrying it, I expect to move us,” Holt said. “If the throw comes my way, I expect to finish the catch. Being useful in one part of the offense doesn’t excuse missing the other part.” It was a direct answer from a player whose afternoon made the claim easy to check.

body.alt: Breloom #98, Porygon-Z #30. Breloom and the Mossdeep defense held Sunyshore to 170 total yards. A defensive preparation illustration.
body.caption: Breloom and the Mossdeep defense held Sunyshore to 170 total yards. A defensive preparation illustration.

body.text: Sunyshore earned its second-quarter stops

Don Philliams brought Marino down for a five-yard loss on second-and-one at the start of the second quarter. Scol Alexander broke up the following deep-right throw to BeckhmJr, forcing Mossdeep’s first punt. The Starseekers had turned an apparently favorable down for the offense into a defensive stop. That is a sequence Karson Jones can use in preparation without pretending the complete performance met the same standard.

The next Mossdeep possession included a twenty-one-yard completion to BeckhmJr on third-and-nine. It also included a Shawn Mareman fumble recovered by teammate Gronkaludon, another Alexander breakup and a Mareman run stopped for a loss. Vinathorn punted again. Mossdeep retained the fumble, so the turnover ledger correctly shows no lost fumbles for either club; the possession still contained mistakes Dorrill has reason to revisit.

Marino then moved the Eclipse forty-four yards before a deep-right pass was intercepted by Castform with fifty-nine seconds remaining in the half. Sunyshore advanced thirty-three yards on the ensuing possession, and Ampharos made a sixty-yard field goal with eleven seconds left. That kick supplied all three Starseekers points. Their defense had created an opening, and Ampharos finished the possession with a sixty-yard kick.

“You can see the standard in those stops,” Jones said. “Now you have to carry it into the next series, and the offense has to make something of it. I’m not sending those guys home thinking three points is who we are. I’m sending them home knowing what three points makes us fix.” Sunyshore’s five first-half punts help explain why the defensive work could only narrow the deficit.
Two third-quarter possessions settled the result

Mossdeep opened the second half with ten plays and eighty-one yards. Holt converted third-and-one with a ten-yard run up the middle during the possession. Marino found George Kipple short right for four yards on another snap, while Gronkaludon caught short-right throws for thirteen and nine. BeckhmJr finished the drive with a four-yard touchdown catch short left at 3:00, and Vinathorn’s kick made it 20–3.

Electric Berry intercepted DeZhaun Watzon’s deep-left pass on Sunyshore’s next possession and returned it eleven yards. The Eclipse needed six plays to cover the remaining fifty-two yards. Marino converted third-and-one with a two-yard run, then found Jones deep middle for thirty-two. Holt eventually scored up the middle from seven yards with thirteen seconds left in the quarter. Mossdeep had added fourteen points while the visitors remained on three.

Jones caught every pass directed his way. His thirty-two-yard reception on that scoring possession was the largest of his six catches, but his later twenty-seven-yarder would solve another difficult down. BeckhmJr finished with four catches for seventy-eight yards and a score; Gronkaludon caught six for fifty-six. The distribution matters because Sunyshore did produce three pass breakups from Alexander and two sacks from Philliams. A few successful individual matchups did not close the other available routes.

“The next throw matters more than explaining the last one,” Marino said. “We had a bad finish to the first half. The answer was to complete the next possession properly.” His twenty-one completions and one interception support a good overall passing afternoon, while leaving room for the specific correction the coach will demand.
The defense and the final 4:54

Joey Sporeter recorded two sacks and seven pressures. Will Shells supplied the third sack, and Watzon finished thirteen of twenty-six for 122 yards with one interception. Myles Gabite ran twelve times for forty-eight yards; the Starseekers’ entire rushing total was also forty-eight. Sunyshore converted three of ten third downs and finished with nine first downs. Fera LaGatr’s five catches for fifty-six yards led the receiving group.

The visitors’ final possession traveled sixty-one yards in ten plays but ended on downs. Mossdeep took over with 4:54 left and never returned the ball. Holt opened with runs of thirteen and fifteen yards. Philliams later sacked Marino for six, creating third-and-sixteen; Marino answered with the twenty-seven-yard deep-right completion to Jones. A later fourteen-yard Holt run renewed the downs again, and the last recorded carry left the Eclipse close to the goal line as time expired.

body.alt: Ninjask #46, Serperior #39. Ninjulio Jones gained twenty-seven yards on third-and-sixteen during Mossdeep’s final possession.
body.caption: Ninjulio Jones gained twenty-seven yards on third-and-sixteen during Mossdeep’s final possession.

body.text: That final drive covered eighty yards without adding points. It was valuable because Sunyshore had no further opportunity to reduce the margin. Mossdeep did not have to ask its defense for another stop or expose the result to a sequence of quick possessions. Jones’ third-down catch was especially useful: it preserved the drive after one of the visitors’ best defensive plays.

Sunyshore is now 11–4 and heads to Pastoria with its division title already secured. Mossdeep hosts Sootopolis before closing at Lavaridge. The bye allows the Eclipse to know where their postseason begins, but it does not settle who they will face or how cleanly they will play. Holt’s two scores, Jones’ perfect six-target afternoon and a defense that conceded no touchdowns supplied the victory. The two punts and the intercepted pass remain available for Dorrill’s next meeting.

art.alt: Simipour #19. Poury Holt supplied 168 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in Mossdeep’s 27–3 win.

articles.title: Lamb goes for 350 as Saffron overwhelms Blackthorn, 70–0
articles.dek: Archam Manning threw seven touchdown passes, HeeDee Lamb caught five of them, and NeMarcus Tare recorded seven sacks. A stunned division leader now has to recover before Mahogany.
articles.author: rowan-vale

body.text: HeeDee Lamb caught thirteen passes for 350 yards and five touchdowns. Archam Manning threw for 528 yards and seven scores. NeMarcus Tare recorded seven sacks. Saffron beat Blackthorn 70–0, and every attempt to summarize the afternoon seems to omit another number that would ordinarily lead a game report. The Dragons arrived as an eleven-win club. They left without a point and with ten sacks charged to their quarterback.

Saffron improved to 12–3, while Blackthorn fell to 11–4. The Psi Corps scored twenty-eight points in the second quarter and another twenty-eight in the fourth. Their 648 total yards exceeded the Dragons’ 179 by 469. They made twenty first downs to Blackthorn’s six, converted six of ten third downs and punted once. Octillery made all ten extra points, providing the afternoon’s most repetitive job description.

The timing made the result especially striking. Saffron had lost 36–33 at Mt. Silver the previous week after an enormous comeback ended with a late field goal. Tare recorded seven sacks in that game too. This time the pressure came with an offense that repeatedly finished possessions and a defense that never surrendered a scoring answer. The same pass rusher had a much more comfortable scoreboard to consult.

“I wanted them to bring the effort back and clean up what hurt us,” Trent Scarboro said. “That’s what I’m proud of. The receiver finishing, the quarterback putting it there, the guys getting home, everybody helping the next guy do his job. You don’t get a day like this from one player, even when one player’s line looks like that.”
The first quarter gave little warning of seventy

Saffron led only 7–0 after the opening period. Gengar Pickens scored on a four-yard run right to complete an eight-play, sixty-nine-yard drive. Blackthorn had punted on its first two possessions, with Pawmo and Tare each recording a third-down sack. The Psi Corps then punted themselves after a drive gained no yards. There was still a recognizable game, with the visitors one successful possession away from changing its direction.

Blackthorn’s next series traveled twenty-eight yards and ended with a missed field goal early in the second quarter. That would be its only field-goal attempt. Saffron responded with a six-play, fifty-two-yard drive, finished by Dam Skattebo’s eight-yard run left at 3:55. The score became 14–0. The Dragons still had time to recover, but their next possessions put them back in precisely the situations Tare was already exploiting.

The shutout therefore did not require Saffron to score on every opportunity. Its lone punt came while the game was still close, and Blackthorn had a kick to put points on the board. The difference grew when Saffron turned successive stops into touchdowns while the visitors continued surrendering possessions. A scoreboard this large can obscure the period when the next stop or completion would still have mattered considerably.
Three Lamb touchdowns before the break

Manning was sacked for five yards at the start of Saffron’s next scoring possession. On second-and-fifteen, he threw deep left to Lamb for an eighty-five-yard touchdown. The drive lasted two plays. Blackthorn had created the long-yardage down and then surrendered the longest reception of Lamb’s afternoon. It was an immediate, costly failure to convert a defensive success into a completed stop.

body.alt: Alakazam #6, Heliolisk #11. Archam Manning and HeeDee Lamb connected on an eighty-five-yard touchdown pass.
body.caption: Archam Manning and HeeDee Lamb connected on an eighty-five-yard touchdown pass.

body.text: The Dragons went backward on their next possession and punted. Manning threw incomplete on the first play of Saffron’s answer, then found Lamb deep right for a forty-eight-yard touchdown at 1:42. Another Blackthorn series began with a seven-yard Tare sack and ended with a punt. Saffron now had the ball with 1:16 left and enough time to add another touchdown before halftime.

That third scoring drive was longer: seven plays and sixty-two yards. On fourth-and-three, with nine seconds remaining, Manning found Lamb deep right for twenty-four yards and another score. The extra point made it 35–0. In less than two and a half minutes of game clock, Lamb had scored from eighty-five, forty-eight and twenty-four yards. Two of those receptions came on the right; the first had gone left. Blackthorn was losing the matchup across the field.

“The distances change. The catch still has to be finished,” Lamb said. “Archam put the ball where I could work. I tried to keep the next route as clean as the last one.” His calm explanation was considerably shorter than the list of touchdowns. The thirteen catches came on seventeen targets, leaving him room to discuss four unsuccessful throws if Scarboro needed another meeting topic.
Tare kept removing the next possession

Tare’s seven sacks came with thirteen pressures. Chen Norton Jr added two sacks and four pressures, while Pawmo contributed a sack of his own. Hatterene finished fifteen of twenty-eight for 154 yards, threw two interceptions and took all ten sacks. The passing-yard total and sack losses are separate recorded figures; the Dragons’ offense was being pushed backward in addition to struggling to complete its throws.

The fourth-quarter sequences were particularly punishing. Tare sacked Hatterene on first-and-ten and then again on fourth-and-one during a possession that ended on downs. Norton recorded sacks on consecutive snaps of the following Blackthorn series. After Saffron lost a Skattebo fumble, Tare answered with sacks on first-and-ten and second-and-seventeen. The Dragons could force a turnover and still find themselves punting within a few plays.

body.alt: Ninetales #42, Hatterene #12. NeMarcus Tare recorded seven sacks against Blackthorn.
body.caption: NeMarcus Tare recorded seven sacks against Blackthorn.

body.text: Blackthorn converted only two of twelve third downs. Its nine rushing attempts produced twenty-five yards, with Sawsbuck gaining fourteen on three carries before appearing on the injury report. Tinkaton supplied six catches for seventy-four yards, the clearest productive receiving line on an otherwise grim offensive sheet. Those completions never became a touchdown drive, and the defense was repeatedly returned to the field against Manning and Lamb.

“Our protection has to give the offense a chance to finish a series,” Clair said. “The score is there for everybody to read. We need to be exact about what happened before each possession ended.” There is plenty to examine without pretending every sack had the same cause or assigning a missed responsibility the record does not identify.
Saffron continued finding different finishers

Pawmo caught a sixteen-yard touchdown pass short left on Saffron’s opening drive of the third quarter. Jolt Train Ln then intercepted Hatterene and returned the ball thirty-one yards. The Psi Corps used twelve plays to cover forty yards on the ensuing possession, with Skattebo scoring from two yards on the first snap of the fourth quarter. The pace varied; the scoring outcome did not.

Manning’s other sack also preceded an immediate touchdown answer. Whiscash brought him down for eight yards, making it second-and-eighteen. Manning found Mothel Irving deep left for forty-six yards and a score on the next snap. Irving caught all five of his targets for 114 yards. With Lamb commanding the largest share of attention, Saffron still obtained another hundred-yard receiving performance and a touchdown from a different player.

Lamb added touchdown catches of twenty-six and twenty-four yards in the final sixty-one seconds. Between them, Seadra fumbled after a short completion and Kecleon recovered for Saffron. Jolt Train Ln intercepted Blackthorn’s final pass as well. Manning finished twenty-five of thirty-three without an interception. Skattebo ran for eighty-two yards and two scores; Pickens’ opening rushing touchdown completed the three ground scores alongside seven through the air.

The final report lists Sawsbuck with six weeks of injury recovery remaining. Saffron’s Skattebo and Tare appear with minor entries in the game record, which should not be inflated into a longer absence or a diagnosis. Blackthorn’s immediate concern is the trip to Mahogany and a division race that remains open. Saffron goes to Cerulean, still pursuing the conference’s top seed while Mt. Silver retains control of its own route to the bye.

Seventy points will move opinions, including mine. It should also leave the specific evidence visible: explosive throws after sacks, seven passing touchdowns, relentless pressure and no Blackthorn touchdown to interrupt the sequence. Saffron has supplied an emphatic response to last week’s defeat. Blackthorn now has two regular-season games to supply one of its own.

art.alt: Heliolisk #11. HeeDee Lamb caught five touchdown passes in Saffron’s 70–0 victory.
